    RUNVIS // LIVE COACHING DEMO

    Today's run,
    with a coach.

    From here on, scrolling is running. Scroll down and a 5km run begins — the distance, pace and heart rate at the bottom move with you. See for yourself when, and why, Runvis speaks up — and when it stays quiet.

    The numbers on this page are sample data for the demo · the real app runs on Apple Watch sensors

    This demo runs in kilometres only. The app itself follows your device's unit setting — splits every 1 km or every 1 mile, with the distances and paces on screen and in the voice in that same unit.

    Every coach cue below is tagged Free or Subscription. Recording, laps, saving to Apple Health, browsing your history, viewing the training plan, the detailed run report and the warm-up screen are all free.

    SCROLL TO START ▾
    SEGMENT 00 — FRONT DOOR · 05:52 AM

    Before you run,
    the coach speaks first

    One tap on start and it flows from weather briefing → warm-up. No server of ours — right on the watch.

    Subscription

    "Hi, this is Runvis. Ready to run together? Weather in Yeouido-dong. It's 26 degrees Celsius with 78 percent humidity. Hot and humid — evaporation is working against you. Hydrate per sports-science guidance: 150–200 milliliters every 15 minutes, roughly every 3 kilometers. Small sips, spread out. That's the briefing. Tap Start Warm-up on screen and let's loosen up."

    WHY · Your neighbourhood name + live Open-Meteo weather → a hydration guide built from the sports-science temperature × humidity rule. On hot days the in-run drink reminders come closer together too. The weather screen and the warm-up timer are free; having this read aloud is the subscription
    WEATHER
    26°C

    78%
    WARM-UP

    For the weather, rounded coordinates go to Open-Meteo; for the neighbourhood name, your current coordinates go to Apple location services, only at that moment.

    SEGMENT 01 — 0.0 → 1.0 KMFree

    No button needed.
    Run, and it knows

    Finish your warm-up and simply start running — Runvis detects the run automatically and begins recording and coaching.

    Subscription

    "Today's condition briefing. You slept 7 hours 24 minutes. Resting heart rate is below your baseline — a good sign."

    WHY · The wrist accelerometer rhythm detects the run automatically and starts recording (free) · The condition briefing comes 8 seconds after the start, and only when resting HR is 5 above or 3 below your baseline, or you slept under 6 hours. On an ordinary day it says nothing

    SEGMENT 02 — 1.0 → 2.5 KM · THE CLIMB

    A hill you see coming
    is nothing to fear

    Load the race GPX course and Runvis warns you about the climb you can't see yet.

    ELEVATION PROFILE — AHEAD 1.5 KM▲ +34 m
    Free

    "In 300 meters, an 800 meter climb begins. Average grade 4 percent. Shorten your stride and hold your rhythm."

    WHY · It reads the course elevation ahead. With the coach on, it uses grade-adjusted pace on climbs to tell you whether your current speed is okay
    SEGMENT 03 — 3.0 → 4.0 KM · FATIGUE SETTING IN

    When the going gets hard,
    it steps in with evidence

    Not "your form is bad" — a coach who tells you what changed, and by how much.

    Subscription

    "Your steps are 5 percent slower and ground contact 7 percent longer than when you started. Shorten your stride and your turnover — and your form — will come back."

    WHY · when two of cadence, ground contact and vertical oscillation drift together, or one drifts far · and only on flat ground at a steady pace, sustained for 30 seconds
    Subscription

    "Good — your form is coming back. Hold that feeling just a little longer."

    WHY · Only on a run where you actually heard the warning · Once, two minutes after the warning and only when the drift has fallen clearly below its peak. If the spacing rule swallowed the warning, no praise follows either
    CADENCE
    166→174
    CONTACT
    252ms
    FORM
    RECOVERING
    SEGMENT 04 — 4.0 → 4.5 KM · WALK BREAK

    Walking is
    part of the training too

    If you're spent, walk. Runvis doesn't call it stopping — it works through the recovery with you.

    Subscription

    "You've started walking — catching your breath is a good call. Jog again when you feel ready, or keep walking if you need to. I'll let you know when your heart rate drops to zone one."

    WHY · It counts as walking when the speed drops into the walking band and cadence stays under 130 for 8 seconds — outdoors with GPS, after the first 5 minutes, and only on a free run rather than a prescribed plan. The moment the walk starts, the running cues still queued are dropped
    Z3151
    Z2138 ← now
    Z1WAITING…
    Subscription

    "Your heart rate has recovered. Ready to run again? Start easy."

    WHY · While you walk it calls out every zone your heart rate drops through, and once you reach zone one it tells you it's fine to run again — you hear the recovery happen
